title: End of the school band and smaller jobs with Kid Sheik
summary: The big band broke up around 1949; Ford turned to smaller groups with Sheik and the Handy Brothers, playing popular tunes that were not yet labelled Dixieland.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah, we had an energetic guy and he's a good hustler and he's a good talker, if you know him. And he can, he's good at finding work. Oh, yeah. So he talked, he talked the president into using the band, if he could get to, if he listened to it. But at this time he was just coming into this and the bands, well the band we had wasn't well known. And we wasn't, we waked up to, we played, we played Autocrat Club, a dance, we played Booker T. Washington Prown, and we played prongs for different schools. The band lasted about, I'd say, to 49 when they broke up. Because Hogan went in the Army and a couple of the other guys went in the service. And I found that I could do better playing with a smaller band, I could make a few dollars more, because we might work once a month at the most. And I was out of school and I was trying to help with the expenses in the house, because we, it was five of us, you see. But I'm the only one that played, my father was sick. And my uncle would get maybe two jobs for me a week, so I just had to leave the band, I see. And I would get into where I could play a little better. And we'd play, I'd play with, I'd play with a guy like Sheep when they have something, and the Handy Brothers, they would get something, I'd play with them. So you were playing both Dixieland and- Well yeah, if you would call it that. But at the time, I just, yeah we just played, well Sheep played the same way he played, but they weren't, they weren't labeled as they do now, just would play it. It wasn't saying he's playing Dixieland.
I would just have called it music. Music, yeah.

But they would play the tunes at the time, because it was, once it hadn't been too long that people were playing those tunes as everyday music. But now it's like Dixieland or Rock or something, but they didn't have all that. And Sheep, we played, like Caldonia was a blues out then, the closest thing to rhythm and blues. We played Caldonia. Yeah. And we might have played, at the time I didn't know Musgraat and Rambo, but we played tunes of that order. Musgraat and Rambo, like played the Sheik of Araby, and we played Lady Be Good, everybody played Lady Be Good at the time. And Can't Escape from You, that's another tune they played. And we played tunes like that, and they played Caldonia, or whatever was out on the the jukebox, like Caldonia was a- You played like the, you know, one of the jukebox hits were out on the- Yeah, but that was also with the same band. That's right. So you couldn't say it was a Dixieland band. Do you speak French? No. Not at all. Neither does my mother. And we would play and finally I got so that things got kinda bad. I wasn't. The most we could make around here was eight dollars, ten dollars a night, and I got married.
